proposal.title: 1978–79 external peripherals — peripheral interfaces and expansion backplanes 1
proposal.reason: Import 12 distinct commercial identities from research items 2, 3, 4, 5, 12, 14, 15, 23, 45, 46, 48, 52. Describe the native host boundary and assess product and core-standard impacts at 1979-12-31. Dedicated memory and other unrelated accessories explicitly carry no direct impact. Conditional comparisons do not establish qualified adapters, provider adoption or measured sales. Prices and cumulative sales remain editorial evidence, outside foundation and the annual-sales model. See the per-item evidence in data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-peripherals-1979/assessment.json. Revised for explicit product/standard relationships: consolidate descriptions into specification, relocate impact prose, compare canonical implementation boundaries and retain source/qualification limits. Historical documentation cannot establish fictional implementations or measured adoption. Per-record evidence: data_storytelling/review_evidence/external-impact-revision/assessment.json.

specification.description: Parallel printer connection using a host-specific interface card and firmware. The intended host environment is {host}. Interfaces, cabling and software must match that configuration.

impacted_standards.assumption_description: Assess {historical_product} in its recorded {host} configuration. Compare alternative Apple II peripheral attachment choices available by the end of 1979; retain native 6502 drivers and required cabling.
impacted_standards.comparison_description: The board retains its native peripheral signalling and software; only functions actually supplied by both purchase paths overlap. Neither the connector nor an adapter implies FlexiBUS device discovery or class compatibility. The relationship concerns alternative complete configurations, not proven direct compatibility with this standard.
impacted_standards.outcomes_description: Working native attachments can reduce immediate demand for a new bus. Cross-host reuse could favour FlexiBUS only where the actual device class and host driver are qualified.

impacted_products.assumption_description: Assess the recorded {host} configuration with its required controller, cabling and software. Parallel printer connection using a host-specific interface card and firmware.
impacted_products.comparison_description: The alternative adds two FlexiBUS ports and a Disk II-compatible controller to Apple II using native 6502 drivers. It provides neither a generic serial/parallel port nor Z80/CP/M execution. The canonical implementation is {implementation}.
impacted_products.outcomes_description: For an Apple II buyer needing the function this adapter actually supplies, the established native attachment can avoid a FlexiBUS purchase. The Logix card instead provides two FlexiBUS ports and a Disk II path; it does not transparently replace every native adapter. This is a conditional purchase-path assessment, not evidence of measured market share or superior performance.
